title: A panel section opens and closes instantly and smoothly
goal: User 2026-10-02: 'when I expand and collapse a pane in the right panel, it doesn't animate like other things, and it's laggy to show. It's not smooth and instant. It feels like we had to load a bunch of heavy UX and then show it.' The section header toggles inside withAnimation(.spring(duration: 0.25)) (InspectorSections.swift:617, :690). Theory to test, not assume: the section's body is only built when it opens (if expanded { content }), so opening builds heavy inspector content (colour wells, glass, menus, previews) in one long main-thread pass before the first frame, and the inserted content fades in place rather than the section growing, so the rows below jump instead of sliding.
acceptance: Measured first (signposts or the walk's mainBusy readout, the same way history-filter-switch-speed-walk does) in a picture and a video document: main-thread time from the click to the first frame of opening and of closing, for every section; the report names the slow ones and why
Opening or closing any section starts moving in the first frame after the click: no main-thread pass over 16 ms (heavy content built ahead of time or lazily after the reveal starts, never before it)

The section grows and shrinks in height, revealing its content top-down with a clip, while everything below slides smoothly on the same curve, matching the timeline dock and other panel motion; no fade-in-place, no jump
The chevron rotates on the same curve; Reduce Motion makes it instant
Rapid toggling (5 clicks in a second) never stutters or leaves a half-open section
Walk with pointer clicks on every section header, both documents, records the longest pass per toggle and photographs mid-animation frames
